findings.title: ONLYOFFICE save callback downloads from any URL: no check against the document server origins (SSRF / local file read)
findings.evidence: savedFileUrl(raw) only does `if (u.username || u.password) return null` and rewrites the public origin, then `return u.href`. The `origins` list it is meant to enforce (office.ts:74, 'the origins a callback may name') is never used anywhere. saveVersion (office.ts:332) passes the result to download() -> `fetch(url, { redirect: 'error' })`, and the bytes replace the user's document. Request: POST /api/office/callback/<token> {"status":2,"url":"http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/..."} or "file:///proc/self/environ" (Bun's fetch reads file: URLs) or "file:///data/system/users.json". Then GET /api/download returns the fetched data to the attacker: internal services, env secrets (OFFICE_JWT_SECRET, ADMIN_PASSWORD), users.json.

findings.title: Office callback accepts an unsigned body when the JWT is missing or invalid
findings.evidence: callbackData(): `const decoded = inBody !== undefined ? verifyJwt(...) : serverJwt(request)` then `if (!decoded) return body && typeof body === 'object' ? body as Record<string, unknown> : null`. The route (routes/office.ts:48-49) only refuses when this returns null, so a body with no token and no Authorization header is trusted. The route is exempt from CSRF (context.ts:27). Any user who opened a file in edit mode gets the callback token in the config from POST /api/office/config (editorConfig.callbackUrl). They can send POST /api/office/callback/<token> with body {"status":2,"url":"<anything>"} and no JWT, and the server saves what that URL returns. Together with F1 this needs no document-server secret at all.

findings.title: One-step update installs and runs package code without the password step-up
findings.evidence: The /fetch-and-apply handler has `void body.password` where /apply and /rollback call `await confirmPassword(admin, ip, body.password, 'update-denied')`. It then goes on to fetchPackage(), stagePackage() and applyStaged(staged.id). applyStaged runs smokeTest, which spawns the package's server.js, and then switches releases and calls restartSoon(). POST /api/admin/update/fetch-and-apply {"password":"x"} with only a stolen admin session (plus CSRF token) installs and starts new code. That bypasses the step-up and its lockout, which README line 144 says is checked first.

findings.title: GET /api/download checks only the 'read' permission, not 'download'
findings.evidence: `const a = need({ user, ip }, query.space, 'read')` then returns fileResponse(abs, ...) with the whole file. Every other route that gives out file contents asks for 'download' too: GET /api/content needs 'read','download' (line 137), batch needs 'download','batchdownload', office view needs 'read','download'. Take a visitor with guestPermissions ['read'] (list only), or a user whose publicPermissions lack 'download'. They send GET /api/download?space=public&path=/secret.pdf and get the file they were only allowed to list.

findings.title: CSV export escapes only '=' (formula injection through + - @ tab CR)
findings.evidence: csvCell: `if (/^[=]/.test(s)) s = `'${s}``. The comment above it says = + - @ tab and CR all start a formula, but only '=' is escaped. Attack: an unauthenticated visitor does GET /api/session, then POST /api/login {"username":"@SUM(1+1)*cmd|' /C calc'!A0","password":"x"}. That writes audit user=<username> with action login-failed. The admin's GET /api/admin/activity/export puts that cell into the CSV unescaped, and Excel runs it as a formula.
